title: Concept circuit
pseudocode_txt:
Concept circuit
───────────────

1. INITIALIZE [Q1, Q2]  →  |00⟩
   Every qubit starts at 0.

2. ENCODE [Q2] ← [0.2]  (angle, arcsin_sqrt)
   Encode turns each number into a tilt, so a qubit's chance of 1 carries the data.

3. ENCODE [Q1] ← [0.8]  (angle, arcsin_sqrt)
   Encode turns each number into a tilt, so a qubit's chance of 1 carries the data.

4. SHAKE [Q1, Q2]  →  spread into every possibility equally
   Shake puts each qubit into an even mix of 0 and 1, so all outcomes are equally likely.

5. ENTANGLE Q1, Q2  →  link Q2 to Q1
   Entangle ties two qubits together: after it, their answers are correlated. It works best when the first qubit is already shaken.

6. MARK [Q2] = 0  →  flip the hidden sign of that one answer
   Mark tags the target answer with a hidden minus sign. Probabilities don't change yet.

7. BOOST [Q2]  →  make the marked answer more likely
   Boost uses interference to move probability onto the marked answer.

8. MEASURE [Q1] → classical bits [0]
   Measure looks at the qubits. Each collapses to a definite 0 or 1 and the answer is stored in a classical bit.
qiskit_py:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit
import numpy as np

qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 1)

# ENCODE [q1] ← [0.2]  (angle, arcsin_sqrt)
qc.ry(0.9272952180016122, 1)
# ENCODE [q0] ← [0.8]  (angle, arcsin_sqrt)
qc.ry(2.214297435588181, 0)
# SHAKE [q0, q1]  →  spread into every possibility equally
qc.h(0)
qc.h(1)
# ENTANGLE q0, q1  →  link q1 to q0
qc.cx(0, 1)
# MARK [q1] = 0  →  flip the hidden sign of that one answer
qc.x(1)
qc.z(1)
qc.x(1)
# BOOST [q1]  →  make the marked answer more likely
qc.h(1)
qc.x(1)
qc.z(1)
qc.x(1)
qc.h(1)
# MEASURE [q0] → classical bits [0]
qc.measure(0, 0)

# ── Run on Aer simulator ──────────────────────────────────────────
from qiskit_aer import AerSimulator
from qiskit import transpile
simulator = AerSimulator()
counts = simulator.run(transpile(qc, simulator), shots=1000).result().get_counts()
print(qc.draw(output="text"))
for state, count in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
    print(f"  |{state}>: {count} ({count/10:.1f}%)")
